title: Unexpected result by WHERE on a GROUP BY view with two IN
bug_query: SELECT * FROM v74 WHERE (vout IN (SELECT t0.c1 FROM t0)) AND NOT (vout IN (SELECT t0.c0 FROM t0));
expected: -89807229 (1 row, since the same predicate evaluates to 1)
setup: CREATE TABLE t0(c0 INT, c1 TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(c0));
CREATE VIEW v74(vout) AS SELECT t0.c1 FROM t0 GROUP BY t0.c1;

SELECT * FROM v74
WHERE (vout IN (SELECT t0.c1 FROM t0)) AND NOT (vout IN (SELECT t0.c0 FROM t0));

title: Unexpected result from row-value IN with min()
bug_query: SELECT c1 FROM t0 WHERE (((c1),(c1)) IN (SELECT c.c1, min(c.c1) FROM t0 AS c));

title: Vuln68-49: OR-to-IN Conversion Loses Column Collation in src/whereexpr.c exprAnalyzeOrTerm
bug_query: SELECT t2.val FROM t1, t2 WHERE t1.a = t2.val OR t1.b = t2.val;
expected: hello, world (2 rows), as without the index
actual: 0 rows once the index enables the OR-to-IN rewrite
setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a TEXT COLLATE NOCASE, b TEXT COLLATE NOCASE);

title: Rowid lookup with a REAL key near 2^63 disagrees with = comparison semantics
bug_query: SELECT x FROM t1 WHERE rowid = 9223372036854775808.0;
actual: returns max-int; the OP_SeekRowid path disagrees with the table scan

title: Unexpected results when filtering a RIGHT JOIN over a subquery reading a VIRTUAL generated column
bug_query: SELECT * FROM t1 RIGHT JOIN (SELECT iif(1,b,1) AS v FROM t1) s ON v GLOB '0' WHERE t1.c='x';
setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a INT, c TEXT NOT NULL, b FLOAT AS (a) VIRTUAL);
SELECT t1.c, t1.c='x' AS p FROM t1 RIGHT JOIN (SELECT iif(1,b,1) AS v FROM t1) s ON v GLOB '0';

title: unicode(), LIKE and GLOB read U+FFFE and U+FFFF as U+FFFD
bug_query: SELECT id, hex(v) FROM t WHERE v LIKE char(65533);
expected: only row 1 (hex EFBFBD), matching what = returns
actual: rows 1, 2 and 3 - U+FFFE and U+FFFF decode to U+FFFD
setup: CREATE TABLE t(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT);

title: Unexpected results of a row-value IN over a PRIMARY KEY column
bug_query: SELECT count(*) FROM t0 RIGHT JOIN t1 ON 1 WHERE (t1.c, t1.a) IN (('a', 100));
setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a INT PRIMARY KEY, c TEXT);

SELECT count(*) FROM t0 RIGHT JOIN t1 ON 1
 WHERE (t1.c, t1.a) IN (('a', 100));

title: Unexpected results of row-value IN with a multi-column index after ANALYZE
bug_query: SELECT count(*) FROM t0 WHERE (c0,c1) IN (SELECT c0,c1 FROM t0);
setup: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX i0 ON t0(c0, c1);
CREATE INDEX i1 ON t0(c1, c0);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX i2 ON t0(c0);
SELECT (c0,c1) IN (SELECT c0,c1 FROM t0) FROM t0;

title: json_extract returns different subtype under index
bug_query: SELECT json_array((SELECT json_extract(j,'$.x') FROM t1 WHERE a=1));
expected: subtype 74 and [[1,2]], as with NOT INDEXED
actual: subtype 0 and ["[1,2]"] when the index is used
setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a INT, j TEXT);
CREATE INDEX t1_x_idx ON t1(a, json_extract(j,'$.x'));
SELECT subtype((SELECT json_extract(j,'$.x') FROM t1 WHERE a=1));

title: Unexpected result by RIGHT JOIN with a UNIQUE INDEX

WHERE t0.c2 IS (SELECT count(*) FROM t0 AS x WHERE x.c0 = v0.c0);

title: Vuln13: Transitive Constraint Optimization Drops Valid Rows on Mixed Collation Equality
bug_query: SELECT * FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2 WHERE t1.a = t2.b AND t2.b = 'ABC';
expected: 1 row (abc | abc), as with the transitive optimization disabled
setup: CREATE TABLE t2(b TEXT COLLATE NOCASE);

title: Vuln27-8: Transitive Optimization Discards Explicit COLLATE During pLeft Substitution, Dropping Valid Rows
bug_query: SELECT t1.a, t2.b FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2 WHERE t1.a = t2.b AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';
expected: 4 rows (all case variants), as with SQLITE_Transitive disabled.
actual: 1 row (only the exact-case 'Hello'); the derived term loses the explicit COLLATE.
setup:
SELECT t1.a, t2.b
  FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
 WHERE t1.a = t2.b
   AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';

title: Unexpected results of JSON functions with a partial index
bug_query: SELECT count(*) FROM t0 WHERE (c0=json_quote(1) AND json_array(c0)='[1]');
setup: CREATE TABLE t0(c0 TEXT, c1 INT);
CREATE INDEX i0 ON t0(c1) WHERE c0=json_quote(1);
SELECT c0, (c0=json_quote(1) AND json_array(c0)='[1]') AS p FROM t0;
SELECT count(*) FROM t0 NOT INDEXED WHERE (c0=json_quote(1) AND json_array(c0)='[1]');

setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a INT, j TEXT);
